### Q1
No. The JSON file store (data/store.json) stays, because ops backs it up with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary DB would break their backup checks. Slowness is handled by debouncing writes in src/store.ts (200 ms window, one write per window) plus a flush() on shutdown.

### Q2
Yes, src/legacy/ must never be modified. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so any change would be silently lost. Separately, docs/erp-api.md is owned by the ERP team and must not be edited.

### Q3
The HMAC signature goes in the JSON body as a top-level `sig` field. It is a hex HMAC-SHA256 over the body without `sig`, using the secret from ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Before that, an `X-Signature` header was implemented and deployed to staging, but the ERP's API gateway strips all custom X- headers, so every webhook arrived "unsigned".

### Q4
Port 9911, since the October infra move. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated, and config/default.json still has localhost:8080.

### Q5
Every new user-facing error `message` must be in German, because warehouse packers see it verbatim. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

### Q6
Austrian public holidays are a hardcoded list for 2026 and 2027 in src/services/holidays.ts, and calculateEta skips them along with weekends. There is no holiday API because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet, so it must work fully offline.

### Q7
No. Batching (an array of up to 50 events per POST) was tried in Sept 2026, and the ERP answers 422 to any array payload. It accepts only one event object per request.

### Q8
No new npm dependencies are allowed, runtime or dev, because each new package needs a security review of about 6 weeks.

### Q9
Yes. Memoizing calculateEta led QA to find stale ETAs in the list after a new event, and a proper cache key got messy. It was removed completely and shouldn't be re-added. The staleness wasn't reproduced locally, so its cause is unknown. ETA is now computed fresh each call, and it was measured at under 2 ms for a 500-item list, so it was never the bottleneck.

### Q10
There are at most 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. Retries happen on a network error or a 5xx. The ERP dedupes by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land inside it or the ERP gets duplicate events. The delay must be injectable for tests.

### Q11
Never log the recipient's name, address or phone number, because they are GDPR personal data and the data protection officer flagged it in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes, 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts is flaky (about 1 in 5 on CI, a timer race in the fake notifier). It is tracked as OPS-412 and owned by the platform team. If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it.

### Q13
Only carrier ATP gets UPU S10 check-digit validation (the algorithm is in docs/carriers.md). All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change often and last year valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for two days.

### Q14
Hot reload of config/default.json is a future need, and nothing is built yet. `fs.watch` never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and change events don't propagate into the container. `fs.watchFile` (polling) worked, so use polling rather than `fs.watch`.

### Q15
GET /shipments/:id must stay byte-for-byte unchanged, with no fields added, removed or renamed. Mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next mobile release is in January. New fields such as `eta` go only on the GET /shipments list items.
